author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose a PS2 picture that shakes or jitters vertically
summary: Measure whether motion affects the entire frame or only interlaced edges, compare menus with gameplay, control output refresh and video-mode changes, and reject fixes that merely blur the oscillation.
heroAlt: PCSX2 video-mode test image with an incorrect vertical output height before a GS presentation fix

sourceLabels.pcsx2-q3-2016: PCSX2 explanation of improved video-mode and interlace detection
sourceLabels.pcsx2-jan-feb-2016: PCSX2 examples of corrected 576p, 720p, and 1080i output dimensions

blocks.text: Measure whether the frame origin moves

Vertical jitter can describe several different observations: alternating fields displayed one line apart, an incorrect output height, an unstable video-mode transition, external refresh conversion, or a UI element that intentionally animates. Establish a fixed reference line such as a letterbox boundary, menu divider, or stationary horizon. Record a short direct clip with the player motionless and note whether the reference itself moves, whether only fine horizontal details shimmer, and whether the shake begins after entering gameplay or an FMV. Capture the reported video mode, region, aspect treatment, deinterlacing mode, device refresh, renderer, and speed percentage.
Do not call a blurred picture stable. Frame blending can conceal a one-line oscillation while reducing text clarity and adding a double image to every moving object.

items: A menu or paused scene with a straight horizontal boundary spanning much of the screen.
A reproducible transition between menu, gameplay, or FMV where the shaking begins or changes intensity.
Native internal resolution, automatic deinterlacing, normal speed, default aspect ratio, and post effects disabled.
The device fixed to one supported refresh rate with adaptive refresh and television motion interpolation off where possible.
A direct recording that includes several seconds before and after the video-mode transition.

blocks.text: Separate field bob from mode and display instability

items: 1. Cold-boot the title, keep the scene stationary, and use frame stepping or an overlay guide to track the reference line across at least ten frames.
2. Determine whether the whole frame alternates vertically, only thin horizontal details change, or the position jumps once when the video mode switches.
3. Leave the emulator profile unchanged and test one fixed device refresh; repeat at another supported refresh only if the first requires cadence conversion.
4. If the entire frame alternates every field, compare one alternate deinterlacing mode with Automatic using the same stationary reference and a short movement clip.
5. If height or origin changes at a menu-to-gameplay transition, restore Automatic and compare hardware APIs while logging the reported interlaced or progressive mode.
6. Disconnect external display adapters and repeat on the device panel; if the panel is stable, investigate television scaling, HDMI conversion, or refresh negotiation.
7. Return to normal gameplay speed and verify that the apparent stability was not produced by slow motion, frame skipping, or a performance stall.
8. Save a per-game deinterlacing choice only when it passes both reference scenes; otherwise preserve defaults and report the exact video-mode transition.

blocks.text: A true one-line field bob is periodic and affects spatial placement, while a refresh mismatch changes temporal cadence without necessarily moving the frame origin. Incorrect video-mode detection can supply the wrong height or interlace status to the presentation path, especially when a title changes modes between FMV, menus, and gameplay. Testing the internal panel separates emulator output from an external scaler. Tracking a fixed boundary provides measurable evidence instead of relying on the discomfort implied by the word shaking.
A stable configuration must hold the same geometry position without sacrificing cadence or detail.

items: The selected horizontal reference stays on the same output rows during a stationary ten-second sample.
Small text no longer alternates position and retains distinct horizontal strokes.
Camera movement remains evenly paced without frame duplication introduced by a refresh workaround.
Menu, FMV, and gameplay transitions keep correct height, aspect, and centering.
Both a cold start and a return from the tested transition reproduce the stable result at full speed.

blocks.text: Shaking reports that point outside the emulator profile

items: Direct capture is stable but a television image moves: reset the display's zoom, motion, and overscan processing.
The reference does not move but object edges show teeth: use the combing workflow and grade field order during motion.
Jitter begins only when speed falls below full rate: solve the performance bottleneck before selecting a presentation mode.
Every mode changes output height incorrectly at one transition: restore defaults and file a video-mode report with serial, region, and logs.

blocks.text: Return deinterlacing to Automatic, select the previous renderer and device refresh, remove custom crop or aspect adjustments, disconnect temporary display converters, and cold-boot the transition. Archive the reference-line clips with their settings; delete any experimental profile that only hides motion by softening it.
PAL, NTSC, progressive, and interlaced paths are not interchangeable

Regional releases and individual screens within one title may request different vertical frequencies and scan modes. A setting proven on one executable or on gameplay alone must not be generalized to another region or to its FMV path without repeating the transition test.
